title: Orchestrated Optimize Suggestion Auto-Apply with Safety Gates and Manual Approvals
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a safe, auditable auto-apply flow for Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching and KV caching profiles). The feature must be able to: 1) gate suggestions with automated checks, 2) perform staged canary rollouts with configurable ramps, 3) require manual approvals for high-risk changes, and 4) support automated rollback when safety signals breach thresholds. Goal: deliver predictable ~10-40% token cost reductions while guaranteeing latency/quality SLOs and full auditability.

Design decisions and trade-offs: We chose a policy-driven approach (policy objects persisted in the control plane) rather than ad-hoc scripts to allow reuse across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Trade-off: more upfront complexity (policy engine + UI) vs long term maintainability. Canary ramp is conservative by default (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with metric gates at each step (p95 latency, error-rate, decode-quality regression on eval prompts).

Acceptance criteria:
- Admins can opt-in Optimize suggestions for auto-apply with a selected "risk profile" (low/medium/high).
- Canary rollout supports step definitions, time windows, and rollback triggers.
- System halts ramp and alerts if any defined metric exceeds thresholds; automatic rollback occurs if breaches persist for N minutes.
- Manual approval flow via Console and Slack flow; approvals are recorded in audit log and attached to the change event.
- All changes are reversible with one-click rollback and documented in the change history.

Operational signals and thresholds:
- Latency: p95 increase <= +15ms (low risk) or <= +35ms (medium) or <= +70ms (high).
- Error-rate: relative spike <= 0.5 percentage points absolute.
- Quality: automated eval set token-level perplexity/regression alert if BLEU/ROUGE/QA accuracy drops by >2%.
- Cost saving required per suggestion >= 3% to be eligible for auto-apply (configurable per-tenant).

Implementation plan:
1) Policy engine: data model, CRUD APIs, and persistence (DB migration).
2) Safe-applier service: executes config changes to runtime with staged canary control and rollback hooks.
3) Metrics guard: integrate with Console metrics; implement short-lived aggregated checks during ramps.
4) Approval workflow: Console UI button + Slack workflow + signature in audit log (link to design doc).
5) E2E tests and chaos tests (simulate degraded nodes and ensure rollback).

Links to artifacts: Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Auto-Apply+Guardrails; implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-platform/pull/6321; dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize/canary-guardrails.

Risks and mitigation:
- False positives in quality regressions: mitigation by running both static eval set and live sampling with human-in-the-loop for medium+ risk changes.
- Cross-tenant blast radius: isolation via per-tenant policy and no-global-defaults for auto-apply.
- Performance overhead of metric checks: keep checks sampled (1-5% of traffic) during ramps.

Next steps (short-term):
- Complete policy CRUD + DB migration (ENG owner: Rafael).
- Build Safe-applier prototype and wire up the first gating metric (p95 latency).
- PM review of approval wording and thresholds (PM: Lena Park).
